text:
Acme Ops: Hey team — since this morning our app started failing on Redwood API calls. Getting 502 + TLS handshake errors intermittently. No config changes on our side.
Maya (Support): Sorry about that, can you share a failing curl output and the request time? Any proxy/gateway in front of your egress?
Acme Ops: Yep we route through corporate gateway at 10.2.3.1. Example curl: `curl -v --proxy http://10.2.3.1:8080 -H 'Authorization: Bearer <redacted>' https://api.redwood.example.com/v1/generate` output shows `* SSL: TLSv1.2 (UNKNOWN) handshake failure` then `HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway`.
Ryan (SRE): Can you try `openssl s_client -connect api.redwood.example.com:443 -servername api.redwood.example.com -proxy 10.2.3.1:8080` (or tcpdump) to see if SNI is preserved? Many enterprise gateways strip or rewrite SNI/Host.
Acme Ops: Ran `openssl s_client -connect 10.2.3.1:8080 -servername api.redwood.example.com` (gateway takes CONNECT then forwards) — cert returned is the gateway cert (CN=corp-gw.internal). Looks like CONNECT is being intercepted, TLS is terminated at the proxy.
Tara (ProdEng): That explains the handshake errors — Redwood expects end-to-end TLS and client SNI. If the gateway terminates and re-mintificates, it may also rewrite host headers or inject auth headers. Any header rewriting rules?
Acme Ops: They do HTTP header normalization for compliance. Example request headers captured: `Proxy-Authorization: Basic *****` and `X-Forwarded-Host: api.redwood.example.com`. We also see the gateway occasionally removes `CONNECT` tunneling and forwards as plain HTTP to an internal route.
Maya (Support): Two possible customer-impacting behaviors: 1) Proxy terminating TLS + MITM certs causes certificate mismatch ordering at client or causes downstream SNI mismatch at our edge if gateway rewrites the SNI to an internal hostname. 2) Proxy rewriting/removing CONNECT breaks tunnel semantics causing our edge to see plain HTTP with wrong Host header.
Ryan (SRE): Quick repro steps for you to run and share: 
```
# 1) Verify SNI preservation
openssl s_client -connect <gw>:8080 -servername api.redwood.example.com
# 2) Test direct CONNECT tunnel (no intercept)
curl -v --proxy http://<gw>:8080 -x http://<gw>:8080 https://api.redwood.example.com -I
# 3) Capture TCP for TLS ClientHello
sudo tcpdump -s0 -w /tmp/egress.pcap host <gw>
```
If the ClientHello shows `server_name: api.redwood.example.com`, SNI is preserved. If not, gateway is rewriting.
Acme Ops: Sharing pcap and curl logs in DM. We see ClientHello SNI set correctly from the client, but when it reaches the Redwood side the SNI is `internal-gw-host`. So the gateway is swapping the SNI.
Tara (ProdEng): That's definitive. Our edge selects certs/kernels based on SNI; if it sees `internal-gw-host` we route to an internal route and then fail upstream TLS validation -> 502.
Maya (Support): Short-term mitigation: 1) Add an egress bypass rule for `api.redwood.example.com:443` so CONNECT is passed through unmodified. 2) If bypass not possible, configure the gateway to preserve SNI and avoid TLS termination for Redwood domains. Please confirm allowing CONNECT tunnel (port 443) without TLS interception.
Acme Ops: We asked infra to add an exception for `api.redwood.example.com` and disable TLS inspection for that host. They asked what to whitelist for IPs and SNI — what's the recommended allowlist?
Ryan (SRE): Recommended: allow outbound TCP 443 to these hostnames (and corresponding CIDRs if you need IPs): `api.redwood.example.com`, `*.redwood-inference.com` (for model/asset fetch). If you must whitelist by IP, we can provide current egress IP ranges (note: they can change with failover) — better to allow by hostname/SNI and keep CONNECT tunneling intact.
Tara (ProdEng): Also watch for header rewrites that inject `X-Forwarded-Host` or change `Host` header — Redwood expects original Host+SNI. If headers are mutated, you might see 401/403 from auth checks.
Acme Ops: Infra applied bypass for the single domain and disabled TLS interception. Retested and calls are green. No more 502s in the last hour. Thanks.
Maya (Support): Great news — can you confirm the root cause as "enterprise gateway was terminating TLS and rewriting SNI/headers causing CONNECT tunnel break"? We'll update the ticket and note the recommended long-term fix (egress allowlist + preserve SNI or use a dedicated egress proxy that supports passthrough).
Acme Ops: Confirmed. We also asked infra to maintain a short runbook: 1) allow CONNECT passthrough for Redwood domains 2) don't rewrite SNI/Host 3) avoid injecting auth headers for outbound REDWOOD requests.
deploy-bot: Incident note created: `INC-2024-7732` - support escalation closed after customer applied bypass rule.
Maya (Support): Marking this thread resolved. If you run into any flaky latency after adding the exception, re-open and we'll look at TLS session reuse and keepalive settings. :thumbsup:
Acme Ops: Thanks everyone, appreciate the quick turnaround :raised_hands:
